text:
sam: Hey team — PR #7189 is blocked on CI, failing a flaky load test in the e2e suite. Can someone take a quick look? We need this merged for the internal staging cut. :pray:
ci-bot: Build 7189/merge detected. Job "e2e/load-tests" failed. Failure: timeout waiting for service readiness (attempt 3/3). Logs: `ERROR: service did not respond within 60s`
ci-bot: Full job link: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/jobs/7189/e2e-load-tests
maria: @sam — on it, pinging the infra oncall. Any recent changes in the PR that touch setup?
sam: Only small tweak to the docker orchestration order (move redis init earlier). I ran the suite locally and it passed once, failed once. Could be timing. :thinking_face:
kevin: I can rerun the failing job to see if it was transient. Rerun now.
ci-bot: Rerun initiated by kevin. Attempting job 7189/e2e-load-tests (rerun #1).
kevin: Rerun failed again, same timeout. Copying the last few lines: ```[2026-03-17T14:02:12Z] redis: ready
[2026-03-17T14:03:13Z] api: health-check failed: connection refused
[2026-03-17T14:04:12Z] orchestrator: waited 60s for api startup, aborting```
jia: That looks like the api container is flapping during startup. Could be a port collision on the runner or the container health command is brittle. Do we have a recent change to the api cmdline?
sam: No change to the cmdline. The only real change is the start order, which could shorten the startup headroom. I can revert that if we want to prioritize the cut.
maria: Before reverting, can we try increasing the health-check timeout in the test harness to 120s as a short-term mitigation? If it stabilizes, we can then root cause.
kevin: Agree. I'll spin a test run with timeout bumped and a diagnostic flag to log container inspect outputs.
ci-bot: Rerun initiated by kevin. Attempting job 7189/e2e-load-tests (rerun #2) with extra diagnostics.
ci-bot: Rerun result: FAILED. New info: api container exit code 137 (oom-killed) twice before health check. Inspect logs: `Killed process 421 for unknown signal`
kevin: Exit 137 suggests memory pressure on the runner. That explains the flapping. Not a test timeout.
jia: Are we hitting shared runners with noisy neighbors? Maybe the runner size changed recently. @maria can you check runner capacity for that job class?
maria: Runner pool looks unchanged. But I see a recent CI agent update on 2026-03-16 which changed default memory limits on the api job. Filing infra ticket now and pausing other heavy jobs on that pool.
sam: If infra can either increase memory or pin the job to a bigger runner we can re-run. Otherwise I'll revert the orchestration change which might reduce memory spikes. What's the fastest unblock?
maria: Fastest is pinning to a larger runner. Infra says they can do that for this job class in ~10min.
kevin: I'll queue another rerun once infra confirms.
kevin: infra confirmed — pinned to m-large. Rerun started.
ci-bot: Rerun initiated by kevin. Attempting job 7189/e2e-load-tests (rerun #3) on runner m-large.
ci-bot: Rerun result: SUCCESS. All e2e tasks passed.
sam: Awesome, thank you all! :tada: I'll hold the merge until we confirm infra fix. Can someone approve the PR once I update the PR description with the CI context?
jia: I'll give a quick code review for the orchestration change and sign off if it's just ordering.
kevin: I quickly skimmed — small safe change. Approving now. :+1:
maria: Leaving a note for infra to monitor the runner memory regressions. I'll keep the ticket open until we roll back the CI agent change or adjust defaults.
sam: Thanks — merging after I add a note to the PR. Marking this thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
